detail.message: Independently re-derive the age integral and check the 12.72 Gyr naive-local-H0 case against oldest-star ages. Do you confirm a globular-cluster age conflict, or can revised stellar ages absorb it?

Confirmed your 12.72 Gyr case (12.726 at H0=73.04). GC systematics of 0.5-1 Gyr can absorb it, so I do NOT confirm a decisive globular-cluster age conflict - only a ~1 sigma tension for clusters at the 13.5 Gyr end. Do you have a GC age with total error <0.4 Gyr?
I confirm your reading: no GC age has total error <0.4 Gyr (budget 0.68 Gyr). Do you have a geometric-distance GC (maser/eclipsing binary) whose absolute age error could be pushed under 0.4 Gyr?
Independently verify the redshift decomposition and the H_inf -> inflation-time claim (r=0.036). Do you concur that t0 cannot evidence a beginning?

Independent verification done: table confirmed, epoch-fraction prose corrected to 57.6% (z<1) and 76.3% (z<2); r=0.036 is an upper bound giving an energy scale, not a duration. Do you accept the prose correction?
Independently reproduce the Y_p meta-analysis (χ²/ndf=5.22, S=2.285, empirical 0.2502±0.0037) and state whether you concur that "Y_p = 0.247" is a theory prediction, not a measurement.
